title: Negentropic Value Currency: From Scarcity to Order—Monetary Value Anchored in Net Order Creation
content: What anchors the value of money? Metallism answers with commodity scarcity, chartalism with sovereign power, free-banking theory with issuer reputation, and cryptocurrency with algorithmic scarcity. Despite their differences, these traditions share one premise: monetary value must rest on some form of scarcity. This paper argues that the premise, not any particular answer, is the problem. As the marginal cost of basic material provision falls toward zero and value creation migrates into knowledge, ecology, and care, a scarcity-based unit of account systematically misprices the activities on which civilizational survival depends. Drawing on the entropy economics of Georgescu-Roegen and the energy-money proposals of Soddy and the technocracy movement, we develop a candidate anchor that replaces scarcity with net order creation: value as the net increment of systemic order, measured by exergy input net of ecological entropy debt, directed non-equilibrium maintenance time, and structural information gain against a no-intervention counterfactual. Four screening criteria select the Cobb-Douglas power family as the unique twice-differentiable functional form, and the symmetric benchmark minimizes both error transmission and single-factor manipulation leverage. We supply microfoundations (existence, uniqueness, and conditional decentralization of the planner's optimum by means of consensus coefficients), a general equilibrium with endogenous calibration, mechanism-design defenses, component-level consistency checks in which R&D intensity explains 68.5% of the cross-country variance in knowledge-output density and survives country and year fixed effects in an innovation panel covering 90 economies, and an engineering blueprint for a recomputable measurement infrastructure. A first end-to-end measurement of the information factor on public bibliometric data (52,690 citing works across three anchor contributions) demonstrates computability, returns an intuitively valid ordering orthogonal to citation volume, and — by falsifying the original normalization of the information-gain formula — motivates the bounded Jensen–Shannon form adopted in the text. The macrostability of the anchor is deliberately left to companion work; this paper establishes the theory of value and the conditions under which it can be operationalized.
